name: Marsic
description: A star 113 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79043: radius 15.773 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 132.468 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.08) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79043: effective temperature 4934 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.105)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.9 from 2014ApJ...785...94L; the 5 published values span log g 2.7 to 2.9, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79043: distance 112.74 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.062), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 113 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 132 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,934 K, so 15.773 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 79043: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Kappa Herculis
quotes.card: The two components, Kappa Herculis A and B, were 27.3 arc seconds apart in 2000.
quotes.introduction: Based on parallax measurements from the Hipparcos mission, κ Her A is about 113 parsecs from the Sun and κ Her B is 600 parsecs ; more recent parallax measurements suggest that B is around 5% more distant than A.
